2: This Ordinance shall be known as and may be cited as the “Treutlen County Mobile Home Ordinance.”
3:
Whereas, consistent with Georgia Law, the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners has the authority to establish by ordinance or resolution such local rules and regulations, not in conflict with existing State or Federal Law, relating to the health, safety, and welfare of the public;

Now therefore be it resolved that the following rules and regulations are hereby adopted. These regulations shall apply to all unincorporated land located within the boundaries of Treutlen County, Georgia.
5:
Except as specifically defined herein, all words used in this Ordinance have their customary dictionary definitions. Unless otherwise expressly stated, the following words shall have the meaning herein indicated:

- (1) Words used in the present tense include the future tense.

- (2) | Words used in the singular number include plural and words used in the plural number include the singular.

- (3) The word "person" includes a firm, association, organization, partnership, corporation, political governing body, trust and company, as well as an individual.

- (4) The word "lot" includes the words "plot" and "parcel" and "tract".

- (5) The word "building" includes the word "structure".

- (6) The word "shall" is mandatory, not directory.

- (7) The words "county” and “Treutlen County” shall refer to Treutlen County, Georgia, and all of its agents, officers and employees.

- (8) | The word "constructed" shall mean to form by putting together parts.

- (9) The word “tax assessor” shall mean the Chief Appraiser of the Treutlen County Board of Tax Assessors or any employee or agent thereof.
6:
2.2.1 Mobile home (manufactured home) means a dwelling unit fabricated in an off-site facility for instillation or assembly at the building site, bearing a label certifying it constructed in compliance with the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974, as amended, U.S.C. 5401, et seq. (the HUD Code, which became effective on June 15, 1976), and meeting the following development standards:

Structure, when in the traveling mode, is eight body feet or more in width or forty body feet or more in length or, when erected on site, is 320 or more square feet in which is built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used as a dwelling with or without a permanent foundation when connected to the required utilities, and includes the plumbing, heating, air conditioning, and _ electrical systems. The term “manufactured home” shall be synonymous with the term “mobile home” when used in this Ordinance.

2.2.2. On-site sewage management system means a sewage management system other than a public or community sewage treatment system serving one or more buildings, mobile homes, recreational vehicles, residences or other facilities designed or used for human occupancy or congregation. Such term shall include, without limitations, conventional and chamber septic tank systems, privies, and designed to be physically incapable of surface discharge of effluent.
7:
No person shall initially locate any mobile home or relocate any mobile home within the limits of the county where an existing on-site sewage

management system will be utilized, nor will install a new on-site sewage management system, without having first applied for and obtained from the county health department a new construction permit or an existing system approval permit. The county tax assessor's office shall not issue a mobile home location permit authorizing the location or relocation of a mobile home unless a new construction permit or an existing system approval permit is presented to it.
8:
2.4.2

2.4.3

24.4

Mobile homes with installation instructions. The Federal Manufactured Home Construction and Safety Standards Program (24 CFR 3280, 3282, and 3283) requires that all mobile homes be provided with installation instructions covering foundation, anchoring, utility connections, and other items, Such installation instructions shall be utilized for the installation of all new mobile homes in the county.

Mobile homes without installation instructions. -Previously occupied mobile homes, which do not have manufacturer’s installation instruction, shall be installed according to the requirements of chapter 120-3-7. Rules and Regulations for Manufactured Homes. These regulations of manufactured and mobile homes are made and promulgated by the state safety fire commissioners. These regulations are on file in the office of the commissioners of insurance, safety fire department, and are open for public examination and copying. These regulations are also on file in the office of the board of commissioners and are open for public examination, and copies will be provided upon payment of the required fee for copying costs.

Transporting and installing mobile homes. Mobile homes shall be transported and installed by a state licensed dealer or installer. The dealer’s or installer’s name and address shall be provided to the tax assessor when applying for a location permit. Upon completion of the installation, a letter on the installer’s letterhead, certifying that the mobile home has been installed in accordance with the appropriate rules and regulations for installing mobile homes shall be provided to the tax assessors’ office, before an electrical permit will be issued.
9: All mobile homes located or relocated in the county after the enactment of this Ordinance shall be required to be skirted in accordance with the skirting manufacturer’s instructions or the requirements of chapter 120-3-7, Rules and Regulations for Manufactured Homes. Acceptable materials for skirting include masonry, stone, and may not include metal or other materials compatible with the siding of a particular mobile home unit.
10: Stairs and a landing shall be required at all doors for all mobile homes located or relocated in the county after the enactment of this Ordinance. Stairs shall comply with section 1112, Stairway Construction, of the state building code, and must adhere to and be constructed in accordance with the requirements of chapter 120-3-7, “Rules and Regulations for Manufacturing Homes.”
12: No mobile home shall be brought into Treutlen County or relocated within Treutlen County without first obtaining a mobile home location permit. No permit shall be issued to locate any mobile home in Treutlen County that is more than ten (10) years old.
13: No public utility or individual shall connect electrical service to any mobile home in Treutlen County, whether by individual electric meter, or power feeds or drop cords as shared service from another structure, without having on file in the tax assessors’ office an approved electrical permit issued by Treutlen County.
14:
The owner of the mobile home or purchaser of a new mobile home shall make application for a mobile home location permit before the mobile home is transported into Treutlen County. Application shall be made in the tax assessors’ office and without limitation shall include the following:

- (1) Name of titled owner of the mobile home.

- (2) Name of the landowner where the mobile home will be located.

- (3) Tax map and parcel number where the mobile home will be located.

- (4) Mailing address of mobile home owner.

- (5) Physical address where the mobile home will be located.

- (6) Serial number, year of manufacture, manufacturer’s name, model name/number, length, width, color, number of bedrooms, number of plumbing connections, material in outside walls and roofing.

- (7) Name of electric utility provider.

- (8) Name of the licensed installer who will transport and set up the mobile home for occupancy. ;

- (9) Applicant's signature.

Other documents, which shall be required, and shall become part of the application include:

- (a) Copy of a septic tank permit application of existing on-site sewage evaluation form, if an on-site sewage management system is required.

- (b) Copy of a tax receipt, showing taxes have been paid current on the mobile home.

- (c) Tax Assessor's copy of State Form PT-41 Dealer’s Statement of Sale of Mobile Home, and a copy of the sales agreement, if the mobile home is being purchased from a dealer.

- (d) Copy of the title or title application for the mobile home.

- (e) Copy of receipt showing user fees (county landfill fee, green box fee, and ambulance fee) have been paid for the current year.
15: An applicant for a mobile home location permit shall pay a fee of Ten ($10.00) dollars for the permit to be established by the county governing authority. The fee must be paid before the issuance of the permit.
16: Upon the completion of the application for a mobile home location permit as set forth in this Ordinance, the payment of the permit fee, verification of land ownership and physical inspection of the proposed location by the tax assessors, a mobile home location permit shall be issued to locate or relocate a mobile home. The permit shall expire 30 days from the date of issue.
17: There will be a waiting period of up to ten (10) working days after a completed mobile home location permit application is submitted to the tax assessor's office before issuance of an approved location permit. This waiting period will allow the tax assessors’ time to verify the landowner of record and physically inspect the proposed location site for compliance with other county ordinances.
19: After physical inspection and measurement of the completely installed and set-up mobile home by the tax assessors’ office, the tax assessors’ office shall issue and affix a location decal to the mobile home.
20: The decal shall be approximately one inch high and three inches long and shall contain the following information: Treutlen County location permit, Tax map and parcel number home is located on and date issued. The decal shall be in the color deemed appropriate by the tax assessors.
21: There shall be no fee for the issuance of a mobile home location decal.
22: The location decal shall be placed directly above the metal plate certifying the mobile home was constructed in compliance with the National Manufactured Housing and Safety Standards Act of 1974. If the mobile home does not bear such a metal plate, or the decal cannot be placed in any location deemed appropriate by the tax assessors.
24: A mobile home will be defined as a “storage mobile home’ if all plumbing fixtures have been removed from within the home, all sewage pipes removed from the exterior of the home, and all openings left by the removal of fixtures and pipe sealed with plywood or similar material.
25: Upon inspection by a county health inspector or member of the county tax assessors’ staff, the mobile home may be declared a storage mobile home. Once declared a storage mobile home, it may never revert to residential use within the county.
26: A storage mobile home may be relocated within the county provided a location permit is applied for and approved. All parts of Article Two, Three, and Four, shall apply to storage mobile homes, except Sections 2.2, 3.3(9)(a) and 3.3(9)(e).
27: A storage mobile home shall be exempt from sanitation fees, ambulance fees, and green box fees.
29:
The owner of a mobile home of any age shall be required to obtain an exit permit prior to removing said mobile home from the county. Exit permits shall be applied for in the tax assessors’ office. Prior to the issuance of said exit permit, all taxes and user fees must be paid.

6.2 FEES. There shall be no charge for an exit permit.
31: The Chief Appraiser or his designee, the sheriff of the county, the deputies thereof, constables, and all other law enforcement officers shall be authorized to issue citations to violators of any provisions of this Ordinance. Such citation shall state the time and place at which the accused is to appear for trial; shall identify the offense with which the accused is charged; shall have an identifying number by which it shall be filed with the court; shall indicate the identity of the accused and the date of service; and shall be signed by the officer who completes and serves it.
32:
- (a) Any person violating the Ordinance, or any provision hereof, upon conviction, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be punished by imposition of a fine not to exceed $1,000.00, by imprisonment in the county jail for a period not to exceed 60 days, or by both such fine and imprisonment, or up to the limits of any penalty provided by state law.

- (b) No person accused of violating this Ordinance shall be arrested prior to trial, but any defendant who fails to appear for trial shall be arrested thereafter on a warrant of the court, and required to post a bond for his future appearance.

- (c) Violations of this Ordinance shall be tried either by citation as described in Section 7.1 or by accusations. Such proceedings may be tried with or without a prosecuting attorney. The county attorney, or his designee shall serve as a prosecuting attorney.

- (d) Violations of this Ordinance shall be tried in the state court or the magistrate court of Treutlen County.

- (e) Each day any violation of this Ordinance shall constitute a separate offense. Each violation of this Ordinance shall constitute a separate offense.
34: The regulations expressed in this document shall be considered as the minimum provisions for the protection of the health, safety, econamy, good order, appearance, convenience, and welfare of the general public.
35: Whenever the requirements made under authority of this Ordinance impose higher standards than are required in any other statute of local ordinance or regulation, provisions of this Ordinance shall govern.
36: Should any section or provision of this Ordinance be declared by the courts to be unconstitutional or invalid, such a declaration shall not affect the Ordinance as a whole, or any other part thereof other than the part as declared to be unconstitutional or invalid.
37: All Ordinances, or parts of ordinances in conflict with any of the provisions of this Ordinance are hereby repealed.
38: These regulations shall not be constructed as abating any action now pending under, or by virtue of, the prior existing mobile home site permit ordinance, or as discounting, abating, modifying, or altering any penalty accruing or about to accrue, or as affecting the liability of any person, firm, or corporation, or as waiving any right of the county under any section or provision existing at the time of adoption of these regulations, or as vacating or annulling any rights, obtained by any person, firm, or corporation, by lawful action of the county or its governing authority except as shall be expressly provided for in these regulations.
39:
This Ordinance shall take effect and be in full force on and after the date that it is enacted by the governing authority and published in the legal organ of said county for four weeks.

On June 6, 2006 the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners passed a Mobile Home Ordinance, setting forth requirements regarding the movement and placement of mobile homes within Treutlen County. The ordinance further sets forth a minimum age requirement for the installation of mobile homes within the County and creates a permit procedure, prior to delivery, installation and the connection of utilities, requiring a connection to an approved septic system and certain anchoring, skirting, and porch requirements.
